title: Loop — a supper on the physical economy
description:
Loop is an invite-only supper on the recursive patterns behind the physical economy — control loops, feedback loops, scaling laws.

It's for founders and investors working in manufacturing, field services, construction, energy, logistics, defense, and humanoids — the companies where revenue is earned at an address, not a URL.

Most tech dinners happen in the world of bits — SaaS metrics, model benchmarks, ARR curves. Loop is the other table. It's for the people building and backing the companies where revenue is earned at a job site, a factory floor, a warehouse, or an address on a map.

The conversation has one spine: the recursive patterns that govern physical revenue. Control loops. Feedback loops. Scaling laws. The physical world doesn't compound like software — but it does compound. Understanding how is the whole game.

Twelve seats, one long table, a pop-up chef, and natural wine from growers around the globe. Five courses built on a single scaling rule. An Escher print on the menu, a Duchamp quote chosen for each guest, and a quiet personalization on each plate. No decks, no panels, no pitches.

The first Loop, during NY Tech Week, drew twenty-five requests for twelve seats. This is the second table.

Loop is hosted by Allometry — continuous margin intelligence for asset-heavy operators. An agentic operating system sold first as a margin floor: it reads what work actually costs from the systems an operator already runs, checks that a crew can deliver it, and blocks any quote below its floor. Every decision accumulates in a ledger of what each commitment actually earned — and the ledger that prices a quote today is what makes an operator underwritable tomorrow. It runs live at a Québec manufacturer, where it surfaced $300K of margin leak in ninety days. The thesis in one sentence: as intelligence enters the physical world, every worker, asset, and machine still needs an economic policy — which work to accept, at what price, above which floor. Allometry…

Openbase is bringing voice-first building to Venice Beach for LA Tech Week.

What if you could step away from your desk and still direct an entire team of AI agents from your phone?

title: Community Build: Tech 4 Good Hackathon
description:
This event is a part of #LATechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com

---

We are The Sameritan Project, a 501(c)(3) public systems lab testing solutions before adoption to impact our daily lives.

Join us for a hands-on Tech for Good Hackathon focused on building practical solutions to real challenges facing communities, organizations, and cities.
Rather than starting with a technology and looking for somewhere to use it, we'll start with the problem. Participants will be presented with a set of real-world challenges and opportunities sourced from community organizations, civic initiatives, and other partners. From there, teams will bring their technical, design, data, product, and creative skills to develop solutions that could move beyond the hackathon and into the real world.
Challenges may include areas such as food systems, civic infrastructure, climate and energy, community resilience, and the upcoming LA28 ecosystem. One potential challenge, for example, is developing tools to better route and coordinate resources across a fragmented network of organizations — a problem that becomes increasingly important as Los Angeles prepares for major events like the 2027 Super Bowl and 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

Whether you're a software engineer, data scientist, designer, product thinker, researcher, or someone with a different technical or creative skillset, you'll have the opportunity to collaborate with others, work directly on a defined problem, and build a tangible prototype.

www.goodsameritan.org

title: The 10x Engineer Showed Up. The 10x Organization Didn't.
description:
A private breakfast for engineering leaders · #LATechWeek Presented by Workflow Builder (by Synergy Codes) and Tentaro

Your engineers are shipping more than they did a year ago. Agents write the boilerplate, review the diffs, open the PRs. Ask anyone on the team and they will tell you they are faster. Now look at the roadmap. Same quarters, same slips, same three things that were almost done in June.

The leak is not in the tooling. It is in two places nobody owns. First, none of it knows your system. Why the service is split the way it is. What the workaround in the billing path is protecting. Which decision from 2021 you are still paying for.

That context lives in four people's heads and it does not scale to agents. Second, the faster the output, the more of it queues behind a human who has to say yes — and there is no structure for that. Approval becomes the bottleneck you built to remove a bottleneck.

This is a conversation, not a talk. No slides, no demo, no pitch. Twelve seats, seven of them for guests, and everyone at the table runs an engineering organization and has already hit this.

Saturday morning, before Tech Week gets loud.

title: TradingDayEvent
description:
Step off the screen and into the room. Hosted by Silwal, this session brings together active equity, options, and futures day traders, scalpers, and execution tool builders during #LATechWeek.
Trading is won and lost in milliseconds, slippage, and psychological discipline. While retail trading communities stay stuck on social feeds, this gathering focuses on the reality of intraday market mechanics: direct-market access (DMA) routing, real-time Level 2 & time-and-sales tape reading, automation tools, and the shifting liquidity dynamics of modern markets.
Whether you trade discretionary size at the opening bell, build automated intraday scripts via broker APIs, or scale algorithmic bots, come talk shop with operators who live in the tape.
What We’re Covering
Market Open to Close Mechanics: Live discussion on navigating opening imbalance, volatility spikes, and avoiding predatory routing/slippage.
Tech Stack for the Modern Day Trader: How active traders are leveraging low-latency broker APIs (Alpaca, Tradovate, Interactive Brokers), Level 2 visualizers, and customized hotkey setups.
Fireside with Silwal & Active Traders: Honest breakdown of risk parameters, max-daily-loss killswitches, and moving from discretionary click-trading to systematic hybrid execution.
Trader Lounge & Open Mixer: Drinks, bites, and candid networking across the LA day trading and fintech ecosystem.

This event is a part of #LATechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com.

title: AI, FILM & THE NEW ECONOMICS of CREATIVITY
description:
AI is making creative work faster, cheaper, and more abundant than ever.

But when almost anything can be generated in seconds, what becomes more valuable?

We already pay more for handmade goods, artisan food, and experiences where craftsmanship and human effort matter. Could creativity be next? Will “Made by Humans” become a premium — or, if the final result is just as good, will audiences simply choose what is cheaper and faster?

Join us for a candid, collective conversation bringing together filmmakers and creators, AI builders and technologists, investors, and the audiences who ultimately experience and pay for their work.

We’ll explore:

When does AI empower a creator — and when does it replace one?
Does knowing how something was made change how much we value it?
Would you pay more for something created by humans?
If AI lowers the cost of creation, where does the value move?
Could “Made by Humans” become the next mark of craftsmanship?
And in the AI gold rush, how do we capture new opportunities without losing the originality and human connection that make creativity matter?

This won't be a conversation where experts talk and everyone else listens. Your perspective is part of the discussion.

Creators tell us what they want to preserve. Technologists show us what is becoming possible. Investors help determine what gets funded and scaled. And audiences ultimately decide what they watch, love, share — and pay for.

The People Who Make × The People Who Build × The People Who Experience

The future of creativity won't be shaped by any one group alone.

We're bringing these different perspectives into the same room to explore what human creativity is worth in an age when machines can create too.

Our Speakers

title: Build an AI workflow editor, natively in Angular
description:
Every AI stack needs a canvas to see and shape what agents do. Almost none are built for Angular. Let's build one, live. Workflow editors are suddenly everywhere: n8n, Dify, LangGraph, a wave of agent builders.

Nearly all of them are built for the web at large. If your team lives in Angular, there's almost nothing off the shelf. In this hands-on session we go from an empty canvas to a working editor for agentic workflows using ngDiagram, an open-source Angular diagramming library.

We cover the patterns you have to support (chaining, routing, parallelization, reflection, human-in-the-loop), demo the finished editor first so you see the target, then walk the code behind it, just a handful of components, to show the leverage the library gives you over a canvas built from zero.

title: AI, FILM & THE NEW ECONOMICS of CREATIVITY
description:
AI is making creative work faster, cheaper, and more abundant than ever.

But when almost anything can be generated in seconds, what becomes more valuable?

We already pay more for handmade goods, artisan food, and experiences where craftsmanship and human effort matter. Could creativity be next? Will “Made by Humans” become a premium — or, if the final result is just as good, will audiences simply choose what is cheaper and faster?

Join us for a candid, collective conversation bringing together filmmakers and creators, AI builders and technologists, investors, and the audiences who ultimately experience and pay for their work.

We’ll explore:

When does AI empower a creator — and when does it replace one?
Does knowing how something was made change how much we value it?
Would you pay more for something created by humans?
If AI lowers the cost of creation, where does the value move?
Could “Made by Humans” become the next mark of craftsmanship?
And in the AI gold rush, how do we capture new opportunities without losing the originality and human connection that make creativity matter?

This won't be a conversation where experts talk and everyone else listens. Your perspective is part of the discussion.

Creators tell us what they want to preserve. Technologists show us what is becoming possible. Investors help determine what gets funded and scaled. And audiences ultimately decide what they watch, love, share — and pay for.

The People Who Make × The People Who Build × The People Who Experience

The future of creativity won't be shaped by any one group alone.

We're bringing these different perspectives into the same room to explore what human creativity is worth in an age when machines can create too.
